name: Joseph Kirchner
headline: Property Management and Consulting Services · Independent Researcher
summary: Property-management professional and independent researcher. Twin Cities leasing, renewals, and site management from 2019; regional management of a HUD-assisted portfolio of 24 PRAC 202/811 properties and 525 units across five states (2023–2024); management of 200+ PRAC 202/811 units across Minnesota (2024–2025). Independent researcher since 2016, part time in linguistics, ethics, and social contract theory, widening from 2020 into the law and the doctrine of qualified immunity; full time since 2025, and the author of an independently published compliance test for separation-of-powers questions and of a history of the immunity doctrine now in draft. Also the owner of a small-business consultancy. Proficient in AppFolio, Yardi, OneSite, and standard office software, with a talent for communication, team leadership, creative problem solving, and refining systems and procedures for efficiency.

experience.summary: Part time from 2016, alongside property management; full time since August 2025. Linguistics, ethics, and social contract theory, with a focus on the Hobbesian and Kantian philosophies (2016–2020); the law, with a special focus on qualified immunity as applied to police officials (from 2020); and, from 2026, a complete genealogy of the doctrine from Floyd v. Barker (1607) to Trump v. United States (2024), with the recovery of its primary-source record at The National Archives (UK) and its commissioned transcription.
highlights: Author of “The Madisonian Separation of Powers Objective Compliance Test” (2026): a six-step objective compliance test for separation-of-powers questions, validated against 36 Supreme Court decisions spanning 154 years

Author of “A Restorative Reading of Genesis 1–3: The Creation Narrative in the Hebrew and Its Versions” (working draft, 2026), cataloguing the discrepancies between the Hebrew, Septuagint, and Vulgate accounts of the Genesis narrative
Commissioned the first transcription of The National Archives file STAC 8/203/38, the record of Floyd v. Barker (1607), by Christopher Whittick, MA FSA, former County Archivist of East Sussex (2026)
